The synthetic company provides document services for internal review.

This controlled synthetic case study describes a proposed document review workflow for a fictional internal team and records an illustrative target of 12.5 minutes for preparing a comparison pack, together with an illustrative baseline of 18.0 minutes that has not been independently measured; these numbers describe planning assumptions only, and the page does not report a completed trial, achieved saving, causal effect, customer result or permission to deploy the workflow.

The fictional team is considering a bounded comparison of two document drafting approaches for its internal review, subject to the access review described in this example; the source leaves the reviewer decision, measurement method, attribution and evaluation window unresolved, and its statement of intended scope does not establish that work has started, that a control is effective or that an operational benefit has occurred.

In a second, entirely fictional comparison described only to test evidence extraction, the page reports a measured duration of 9.75 minutes for three selected packs during one afternoon; it also states that the sample excluded failed drafts, the comparison method was not recorded, and no independent reviewer checked the figures, so the number is a restricted source assertion rather than evidence of a repeatable improvement or a general customer outcome.
